picks.d: SF's biggest EDM weekend is back at Pier 80 and it's an absolute banger of a lineup. Saturday brings Robyn, Fatboy Slim, Dog Blood, and Soulwax. Sunday counters with Swedish House Mafia, Tiesto, Zara Larsson, and Four Tet. Block the whole weekend.

picks.t: Giants vs. Dodgers — Final Home Stand
picks.d: The Giants close out their regular season at Oracle Park against the best team in baseball — the 93-win Dodgers. This is it, the last home games of the year, and every ticket buyer gets a 2027 voucher. NL West drama, bay breezes, and garlic fries. Do not sleep on this.

The jazz-pop sensation with the velvet voice is bringing her lush orchestral world to Chase Center and honestly it's going to feel impossibly intimate for such a big room. Laufey's the kind of artist you discover and then immediately become obsessed with — this is your moment to see her live before she gets even bigger.

picks.t: Sunset Night Market: Autumn Moon Festival
picks.d: Irving Street transforms into a lantern-lit, dumpling-scented dream for the Autumn Moon Festival. DJs, dance performances, food trucks, and the best mom-and-pop shops in the Sunset all come out to play. It's free, it's festive, and it's exactly the kind of only-in-SF evening you'll be talking about Monday.

picks.t: Peter Pan Goes Wrong — Opening Night
picks.d: The Cornley Polytechnic Drama Society is attempting Peter Pan and, spoiler, everything is going to go spectacularly wrong. SF Playhouse opens their 2026/27 season with this wickedly funny comedy that runs through November — but opening weekend always has that extra electric energy. Grab friends and prepare to cry-laugh.

picks.t: Dolly Parton Day — Free Outdoor Celebration
picks.d: San Francisco is throwing a free outdoor festival in honor of the one and only Dolly Parton, and if that sentence doesn't make you smile then I don't know what will. Live music, tributes, and full-on glam energy right in the heart of Union Square. It's free, it's joyful, it's very SF.

picks.t: Erykah Badu at the Greek Theatre
picks.d: The Baddie herself plays the stunning outdoor Greek Theatre in Berkeley on Sunday and this is the kind of show you'll be telling people about for years. Erykah's sets are notoriously unpredictable, deeply spiritual, and completely mesmerizing. Pack a layer, grab a friend, and prepare to be transported.

If you haven't seen Benson Boone live yet, this is your sign. The guy does backflips off pianos and hits notes that make no sense coming from a human throat — it's theatrical, it's emotional, and it goes viral for a reason. A big, fun Wednesday night that'll power you right into the new month.

BTS's RM is sharing his personal art collection — 200 works, many Korean pieces never shown in the US before — alongside selections from SFMOMA's own holdings. Members get first access starting October 1st, ahead of the public opening on the 3rd. If you've been on the fence about a membership, this is your tipping point.

picks.t: Free Shakespeare: Antony and Cleopatra — Final Weekend
picks.w: Through Sun Sep 27 · Sue Bierman Park
picks.d: The 44th season of Free Shakespeare in the Park wraps this weekend and this is your absolute last chance to catch Antony and Cleopatra under the open sky. No tickets, no cost — just show up to Sue Bierman Park and let the drama wash over you. One of SF's most beloved annual traditions.

Kevin, Joe, and Nick are in town for one night and they're bringing the full arena spectacle — lighting rigs, costume changes, sing-alongs, the works. Whether you were a Disney Channel kid or a millennial who secretly knows every word to Burnin' Up, this is going to be a great time. Get your friendship bracelets ready.

picks.t: Joanne McNally: Pinotphile — Cobb's Comedy Club
picks.d: Joanne McNally's wine-fueled, razor-sharp stand-up is one of the hottest touring shows of the year and she's at Cobb's for just two nights. Tickets are almost gone — Friday has 37 left, Saturday not many more. This is a book-it-now situation, not a think-about-it-later one.

picks.t: Circus on the Square — Free Family Fun
picks.d: Circus Bella takes over St. Mark's Square for the 4th Annual Circus on the Square — free performances, free popcorn, and the kind of wholesome Saturday morning energy that makes you feel good about the world. Perfect for families, casual drop-ins, or anyone who just wants some joy with their weekend coffee.

ongoing.d: Citywide artist studio visits every weekend through Oct 25 — free, wanderable, and wonderful.

ongoing.t: Little Shop of Horrors — New Conservatory Theatre
ongoing.d: The cult classic musical runs through Oct 18; perfect spooky-season starter.
Emma Rice's Hitchcock-inspired comic caper is open now on the Geary stage.

ongoing.t: Graciela Iturbide: Between Two Worlds — SFMOMA
ongoing.d: Five decades of the acclaimed Mexican photographer's work, on view through Nov 29.

ongoing.t: Arts of Indigenous America — de Young Museum
ongoing.d: Four new permanent galleries open now; free for Bay Area residents every Saturday.

ongoing.t: FX Harsono: Writing in the Rain — Asian Art Museum
ongoing.d: Closing soon — this video installation on memory and identity is worth catching before it's gone.

new.name: Yumee Katsu
new.d: The beloved South Bay mini-chain makes its SF debut with crispy fish, pork, and cheese-stuffed katsu, plus curry and noodles.

new.type: Indian Coffee Shop · Lower Nob Hill
new.name: Le Mil's
new.d: SF's newest Indian café does cortados alongside chicory coffee with masala jaggery syrup and pastries from Saltwater Bakeshop.

new.name: New Mission Bay Chinese
new.d: Waterfront patio with fire pits, sliding doors, and standout dishes like prawn cocktail with Sichuan peppercorn sauce.

new.name: Sons & Daughters
new.d: Two Michelin stars, a buzzy new Mission address, and a tasting menu that makes you feel like a very lucky person.

new.name: Niku Steakhouse
new.d: A5 wagyu displayed like gallery art, with perfectly charred tomahawks and New York strips in a space unlike any other SF steakhouse.

classic.name: Yank Sing
classic.d: Legendary dim sum institution — the har gow alone is worth crossing town for.

classic.name: La Taqueria
classic.d: James Beard Award-winning Mission burrito, full stop. No rice, just perfection.

classic.name: Cotogna
classic.d: Wood-fired pasta and whole-roasted meats in a room that feels like it's been there forever in the best way.

classic.name: Hog Island Oyster Co.
classic.d: Bay views, killer Marin-farmed oysters, and a cold glass of white wine — that's the whole plan.

classic.name: Turtle Tower
classic.d: The pho ga here is transcendent — clean, fragrant broth and silky chicken that regulars swear by.

bars.name: Vesuvio Cafe
bars.d: Historic Beat Generation haunt with cheap drinks, great people-watching, and zero pretension.

bars.name: Zeitgeist
bars.d: Giant outdoor beer garden, strong pours, and a crowd that actually wants to talk to you.

bars.name: Smuggler's Cove
bars.d: Three floors of rum-forward tiki cocktails in a ship-wrecked wonderland — plan to stay longer than you intend.

bars.name: Starbelly Wine Bar
bars.d: Neighborhood gem with a smart by-the-glass list and a patio that's perfect for a September evening.

bars.name: Monarch
bars.d: Multi-level club with serious DJ bookings, a gorgeous bar, and a dancefloor that gets going late.

bars.name: Slim's
bars.d: Mid-size room with great sound, cold beer, and an eclectic lineup that always delivers.

bars.name: Charmaine's at Proper Hotel
bars.d: Retractable-roof rooftop with city views, strong spritzes, and an after-work crowd that skews fun.

bars.name: Noe Valley Ministry Wine Bar
bars.d: Low-key neighborhood bottle shop and bar — perfect for a relaxed mid-week glass.

games.detail: Regular season finale — NL West drama on full display
Second game of final home stand; 2027 ticket voucher with purchase
Last Giants home game of 2026 — go out on a high note

sports.note: MLB postseason begins September 29 — this is your last chance to see the Giants at Oracle Park this year.
No home games this week — the Valkyries (29–11, 2nd in West) are on the road. Check valkyries.com for potential playoff home dates emerging after Sep 27.

concerts.d: The Icelandic-Chinese jazz-pop phenomenon brings her lush, string-drenched world to Chase Center. Silky vocals, classic jazz sensibility, and a fanbase that genuinely adores her — this one will feel surprisingly intimate for an arena show. Dress up a little. You'll want to.

Acrobatics, soaring high notes, anthemic rock-pop, and a stage presence that genuinely cannot be contained — Benson Boone's live show is one of the most talked-about of the year. He's been selling out venues globally and this Chase Center stop is a big one. Arrive early.

Twenty years of hits, a production that goes all-out, and an audience that knows every single word. Kevin, Joe, and Nick always deliver a genuinely fun arena night — multi-generational, high-energy, and zero irony. This one's pure joy.

Neo-soul royalty at one of the most beautiful outdoor amphitheaters in the country. Erykah's sets roam freely across her catalog and into unexpected territory — you never know exactly where she'll take you, and that's exactly the point. Bundle up, the Berkeley hills get breezy.

concerts.t: Jack Johnson with G. Love — SURFILMUSIC Tour
concerts.d: Sold out both nights, but resale is your friend here. Jack Johnson's mellow acoustic energy at the Greek Theatre at sunset is genuinely one of the most pleasant ways to spend a Northern California evening. G. Love opens. The vibes are immaculate.
concerts.venue: Greek Theatre, Berkeley · SOLD OUT (resale available)

concerts.t: Rusty Chains — Tribute to Chris Cornell
concerts.d: A full night dedicated to the thunderous legacy of Chris Cornell — Soundgarden, Audioslave, and beyond — inside one of SF's most atmospheric rooms. The GAMH's ornate Victorian bones make it the perfect setting for music this big and emotional.
concerts.venue: Great American Music Hall · GAMH Box Office

concerts.d: Late-night 21+ show at the GAMH — underground, edgy, and exactly the kind of thing you'll only find in SF. The Great American Music Hall's intimate room and devoted local crowd make late shows here feel like a special secret. This one goes hard.
concerts.venue: Great American Music Hall · 21+ · GAMH Box Office

concerts.d: The GAMH closes out the week with Los Thuthanaka on the same stage that launched legends. The ornate balconies, perfect sightlines, and intimate scale make every show here feel like a gift — catch them before the word gets out further.
concerts.venue: Great American Music Hall · GAMH Box Office

concertsOngoing.d: Davies Symphony Hall at Van Ness; check sfsymphony.org for this week's program and guest soloists.
Kishi Bashi, Slow Pulp, and Dilated Peoples all coming in late October; check thefillmore.com for the full fall calendar.

singles.d: SF's most reliable speed dating series puts you face-to-face with 8–12 actual humans in one fun, structured evening at Blackbird Bar. Multiple age brackets, a laid-back format, and the kind of low-stakes energy that makes it genuinely enjoyable even if sparks don't fly. Way better than the apps.

singles.t: Lock & Key Singles Mixer — SF Bay Area
singles.d: Women get keys, men get locks, everyone circulates trying to find their match — it's a physical icebreaker that actually works. The Lock & Key format removes all the awkward standing-around-not-knowing-what-to-do energy and replaces it with an excuse to talk to everyone. Smart, social, and genuinely fun.

Volo Sports runs coed pickup pickleball at China Basin Park right on the waterfront — no experience necessary, all levels welcome. It's casual, it's active, and the inherent silliness of pickleball makes everyone relax and actually talk to each other. The best singles scene you didn't know you needed.

singles.t: Vegan Scene Singles Speed Dating — North Beach (Ages 25–39)
singles.d: Same great speed dating format, but everyone in the room shares your values around food and lifestyle — which turns out to be a genuinely great conversation starter. North Beach is a lovely neighborhood for a date-night stroll after, too, if things go well.

singles.t: Glow Kickball + Flip Cup — Volo Sports
singles.w: Thursdays in October · Mission Dolores Park
singles.d: Kick a glowing ball in the park with strangers who become friends by the third inning, then celebrate with flip cup. Volo's leagues are explicitly designed for adults who want to play rec sports and meet people — the social aspect is baked right in. Sign up for a season and commit to actually having fun this fall.

singles.t: Bounce SF & So Sweet: DJ Planet Express — Monarch
singles.w: Check ra.co for exact date · Monarch SF
singles.d: Two crews, one dancefloor, and a euphoric night of Y2K trance, hard groove, and Eurodance that will make you feel like you're in a 2003 music video in the best possible way. Monarch's intimate space and immersive lighting make it perfect for meeting people mid-groove. Check RA for the confirmed date this week.

singlesOngoing.t: Run Club SF — Weekly Group Runs
singlesOngoing.d: Multiple runs weekly across SF neighborhoods — free, all levels, and a genuinely great way to meet people while moving your body.
Updated daily with every club night across 1015 Folsom, Audio SF, Public Works, The Great Northern, and more — your real-time nightlife radar.
Serious house music in one of SF's best club spaces — check ra.co for the confirmed date and RARA tickets.

date.title: Shakespeare Meets Sunset
date.tagline: Theater, twilight, and a very good walk.

steps.title: Golden Hour at the Embarcadero
steps.detail: Stroll the waterfront, grab coffee or a snack from the Ferry Building farmers market, and ease into the evening with zero pressure.

steps.title: Free Shakespeare: Antony and Cleopatra
steps.detail: Head to Sue Bierman Park for the final weekend of free outdoor Shakespeare. Bring a blanket, sit close, and let Cleopatra do the heavy romantic lifting for you.

steps.title: Walk Through North Beach
steps.detail: Post-show stroll through North Beach — Columbus Ave, Vesuvio Cafe for a cheap drink, City Lights Bookstore if it's still open. The city does the rest.

date.title: Laufey Night
date.tagline: Jazz-pop, good food, and a walk along the bay.

steps.title: Dinner at Cotogna
steps.detail: Wood-fired pasta and roasted meats in North Beach — make a reservation, order the wood-roasted chicken, and take your time over a bottle of something Italian.

steps.title: Laufey at Chase Center
steps.detail: Tuesday September 30th — the jazz-pop sensation in an arena that somehow feels intimate. Her voice is extraordinary live and this is a genuinely romantic night out.

steps.title: Nightcap with a View
steps.detail: Wrap the evening at Charmaine's rooftop bar at the Proper Hotel — city lights, good cocktails, and the natural afterglow of a great show.

date.title: Wagyu and Erykah
date.tagline: The full splurge: spectacular dinner, legendary live music.

steps.title: Niku Steakhouse
steps.detail: The Design District's A5 wagyu temple. The butcher shop looks like an art gallery and the beef is extraordinary. Reserve the tasting menu and surrender completely.

steps.title: Drive or BART to Berkeley
steps.detail: Head over the Bay Bridge or hop BART to the UC Berkeley stop — the Greek Theatre is a 15-minute walk uphill through a beautiful campus.

steps.title: Erykah Badu at the Greek Theatre
steps.detail: Sunday September 27th. Neo-soul royalty under the stars in one of America's most beautiful outdoor venues. Bring a jacket. This is a night you will remember.

solo.title: Open Studios Saturday
solo.tagline: Wander the city, meet artists, feel cultured.

steps.title: SF Open Studios Kicks Off
steps.detail: September 26th is the first weekend of the citywide Open Studios series. Download the map at SFOpenStudios.org and pick a neighborhood — no plan required, just wander in.

steps.title: Free Admission at the de Young
steps.detail: Bay Area residents get free general admission every Saturday. The new Arts of Indigenous America galleries are genuinely worth your time. Bring your ID.

steps.title: Golden Gate Park Wander
steps.detail: The de Young is right in the park — take the long way out, find a bench, and just be somewhere beautiful for a while. Solo Saturdays are underrated.

solo.title: Comedy Night at Cobb's
solo.tagline: Great food, great laughs, great use of a Friday.

steps.title: Dinner at Turtle Tower
steps.detail: Transcendent pho ga in the Tenderloin — fragrant broth, silky chicken, and a bill that won't hurt. Sit at the counter and be happy.

steps.title: Joanne McNally: Pinotphile at Cobb's
steps.detail: Friday September 25th — grab one of the last tickets to this nearly-sold-out wine-soaked comedy set. Sitting alone at a comedy show is genuinely one of the best solo activities.

steps.title: Nightcap in North Beach
steps.detail: Cobb's is right on Columbus Ave — walk next door to Vesuvio, order something cheap, and sit in a 70-year-old bar that has no interest in being trendy. Perfect end.

solo.title: RM x SFMOMA Preview + Chef's Dinner
solo.tagline: Art, culture, and a serious meal — treat yourself.

steps.title: Sons & Daughters Lunch
steps.detail: The two-Michelin-star New Nordic restaurant just relocated to the Mission — if they're doing lunch service, this is the move. Otherwise, book dinner and reverse the order.

steps.title: SFMOMA — RM x SFMOMA Member Preview
steps.detail: October 1st is the first day of member previews for RM's personal collection — 200 works, many Korean pieces never seen in the US. This is a genuinely historic museum moment.

steps.title: Smuggler's Cove Nightcap
steps.detail: End the day at Hayes Valley's ship-wrecked tiki wonderland. Order the Painkiller, sit in the crow's nest, and congratulate yourself on a very good solo Thursday.

birthday.title: Dolly Parton Day Birthday Bash
birthday.tagline: The city is literally throwing a party — join it.

steps.title: Dolly Parton Day at Union Square
steps.detail: Thursday September 25th — SF is throwing a free outdoor festival honoring Dolly Parton with live music and full glam energy. Tell everyone it's your birthday and watch the city celebrate with you.

steps.title: Birthday Drinks on Columbus Ave
steps.detail: March the crew to North Beach — Vesuvio or Tony Nik's for the first round. It's your birthday, someone else picks up the tab.

steps.title: Late-Night at Monarch or Great American Music Hall
steps.detail: Head to Monarch for club night or catch the late show at GAMH — Six Sex is playing Friday, Rusty Chains on Saturday. Keep the birthday going as late as you want.

birthday.title: Portola Festival Birthday Weekend
birthday.tagline: Swedish House Mafia and your whole crew. Enough said.

steps.title: Pre-Game Brunch
steps.detail: Start at Hog Island Oyster Co. on the Embarcadero — oysters, white wine, bay views, and birthday toasts before the day really begins.

steps.title: Portola Music Festival at Pier 80
steps.detail: Saturday for Robyn, Fatboy Slim, and Soulwax — or Sunday for Swedish House Mafia, Tiesto, and Four Tet. Get tickets early and get there early for a good spot.

steps.title: After-Party at Monarch
steps.detail: The Portola energy doesn't have to stop at the festival gates — Monarch has house nights running late and the dancefloor stays moving. Carry the birthday all the way through.

birthday.title: Big Birthday Steakhouse + Arena Show
birthday.tagline: The full experience: legendary dinner, arena lights, the works.

steps.title: Niku Steakhouse — The Whole Wagyu Thing
steps.detail: Book the full table at Niku in the Design District. A5 wagyu for the birthday person, tomahawks for the crew, the butcher shop display as your backdrop. This is a meal people remember.

steps.title: Laufey or Benson Boone at Chase Center
steps.detail: Laufey on Tuesday September 30th for a sophisticated, emotionally gorgeous night — or Benson Boone on Wednesday October 1st for pure high-energy spectacle and backflips. Pick your vibe.

steps.title: Nightcap at Charmaine's Rooftop
steps.detail: End on the rooftop at the Proper Hotel with the whole crew, city lights in every direction, and the satisfaction of a birthday done absolutely right.

friends.title: Autumn Moon Festival Friday
friends.tagline: Dumplings, DJs, and the best neighborhood in the city.

steps.title: Sunset Night Market: Autumn Moon Festival
steps.detail: Friday September 25th on Irving Street between 20th and 25th Ave. Free DJs, dance performances, food trucks, and the mom-and-pop shops of the Sunset all showing out. Show up, eat everything.

steps.title: Walk Golden Gate Park as the Sun Sets
steps.detail: The park's western end is right there — take the long walk through as the sky goes golden. Free, gorgeous, and everyone's going to want a photo.

steps.title: Drinks in the Haight
steps.detail: Head east on Haight Street for a round at Toronado (epic beer selection) or Magnolia Brewing — cheap, neighborhood, and the right energy for a Friday night with friends.

friends.title: Circus Saturday into Portola
friends.tagline: A Saturday that earns its own highlight reel.

steps.title: Circus on the Square — Free!
steps.detail: Saturday September 26th at St. Mark's Square — Circus Bella performs for free, there's popcorn, and it's genuinely delightful. Perfect warm-up for the day.

steps.title: Lunch at a Mission Bay Waterfront Restaurant
steps.detail: Hit the new Mission Bay Chinese spot — great for groups, waterfront patio, fire pits on Mission Creek, and a banana buttercake that'll start arguments about who gets the last piece.

steps.title: Portola Festival at Pier 80
steps.detail: Saturday's lineup: Robyn, Dog Blood, Fatboy Slim, Soulwax. Pier 80 is a quick ride from Mission Bay — make it a seamless group migration and dance until your legs give out.

friends.title: Giants Finale + Dinner + Comedy
friends.tagline: The full SF friend-group day — sports, food, laughs.

steps.title: Giants vs. Dodgers — Final Home Game
steps.detail: Saturday September 27th at Oracle Park — last Giants home game of 2026, against the best team in baseball, with a 2027 ticket voucher included. Get there early for the view and the garlic fries.

steps.title: Post-Game at the Embarcadero
steps.detail: Walk off the game energy along the waterfront — Hog Island Oysters for a post-game happy hour, or grab seats at a Ferry Building spot and debrief the whole afternoon.

steps.title: Joanne McNally at Cobb's Comedy Club
steps.detail: If tickets remain — grab them now, they're almost gone. Saturday September 26th at 7pm or 9:15pm. The perfect capper to a full SF day with people you actually like.

steps.title: Circus on the Square
steps.detail: Saturday September 26th, 11am–2pm at St. Mark's Square. Free Circus Bella performances, free popcorn, family-friendly energy. This is genuinely a great morning.

steps.title: de Young Museum — Free Saturday
steps.detail: Bay Area residents get free general admission every Saturday with ID. The new Indigenous American galleries are respectful, beautifully installed, and genuinely interesting for adults at every age.

steps.title: Golden Gate Park Walk
steps.detail: The de Young is right inside the park — take the scenic route out past the conservatory and the tulip garden, let the afternoon wind down naturally, and find a coffee or tea somewhere on 9th Ave before heading home.

steps.title: Ferry Building Morning
steps.detail: Start at the Ferry Building — Hog Island for oysters and chowder, Cowgirl Creamery for cheese, Blue Bottle for coffee. Stroll the Embarcadero and let your parents take photos of the Bay Bridge.

steps.title: Giants vs. Dodgers at Oracle Park
steps.detail: Saturday September 27th — last Giants home game of 2026 against the Dodgers. Get seats with a bay view, order the garlic fries immediately, and explain why the Dodgers are always the villain.

steps.title: Dinner at Cotogna
steps.detail: North Beach Italian — wood-fired and unfussy in the best way. The kind of place parents immediately recognize as a great restaurant without needing to know who the chef is. Reserve ahead.

parents.title: SFMOMA + Symphony + Dinner
parents.tagline: The refined SF experience, done properly.

steps.title: SFMOMA — Graciela Iturbide Exhibition
steps.detail: Five decades of the acclaimed Mexican photographer's work across SFMOMA's beautifully transformed galleries. Give yourselves two hours — it warrants it.

steps.title: Lunch at Sons & Daughters
steps.detail: Two Michelin stars, a bold New Mission address, New Nordic tasting menu. If they're doing lunch service this is the most impressive thing you can possibly do with a visiting parent. They will talk about it for years.

steps.title: SF Symphony at Davies Hall
steps.detail: Check sfsymphony.org for this week's program at Louise M. Davies Symphony Hall on Van Ness. The hall itself — warm acoustics, beautiful design — is worth the visit alone. A genuinely perfect parent-visit evening.
